items.en: Reduces the monthly maintenance supply cost by %s.
A number of crew positions are classified as low-skilled, resulting in a reducation of %s to overall crew salary for this ship.

The ship's performance suffers from competing design priorities, with multiple bleeding-edge projects integrated too late in the design cycle.

The ship's flux dissipation and capacity, even the nominal base values, are reduced by %s, and the effectiveness of its Temporal Shell system is reduced to %s time flow rate.

The range of ballistic weapons is reduced by %s, the rate of fire of missile weapons is reduced by %s, and the flux generation of energy weapons is increased by %s.

On the plus side, extra nanoforge capacity can be brought online more easily, allowing the installation of a %s despite the ship already having a fighter bay, increasing the number of operational fighter bays to %s.

Improves the maximum burn level of the slowest ship in the fleet by 1. Multiple tugs can not be used to speed up the same ship by more than 1.

Cannot be used in combat.
This ship is fully automated, and does not require - and cannot take on - any human crew.

The ship will attempt to recoil (hopefully) away from danger when taking substantial hull damage.

Increases the ship's hull integrity by %s. Crew casualties in combat are increased by %s.

Reduces weapon turn rate by %s, increases recoil by %s, and reduces the durability of all weapons by %s.

Supply cost to recover from deployment reduced by %s.
Increases base range of small and medium weapons in ballistic slots.
Installs basic shields on shieldless ship.
Reduces damage taken by shields and armor by %s for destroyers, and by %s for cruisers.
Increases number of fighter pilots recovered by %s.
Increases the rate of fire of the Lens by %s.
Will target missiles if no other targets are in range.

Paints the target and provides targeting data, increasing all hull and armor damage taken by %s / %s / %s / %s based on the number of tactical lasers hitting the target's hull or armor, with the maximum reached at 4 or more beams.
Each shot deals an additional 1000 damage to armor over 10 seconds. This damage is not reduced by armor, and, when hitting fighters, can leak through to hull once armor is stripped.

A series of ill-advised modifications have been made to militarize this normally-harmless hull. Whether it's more dangerous to its crew or its enemies remains a point of contention at dockside bars, but these modifications are often favored by pirates seeking to create the impression of overwhelming firepower.
